graph.summary: Lorazepam → Gamma-aminobutyric acid receptor subunit alpha-1 → chloride channel activity → membrane hyperpolarization → Anxiety

evidence.snippet: Benzodiazepines bind to a site on the GABA(A) receptor which is different from the GABA binding site, thus increasing the chloride current.
evidence.explanation: Lorazepam is a benzodiazepine that binds allosterically to the GABA-A receptor and increases its activity (chloride current).

paper.title: Identification of molecular substrate for the attenuation of anxiety: a step toward the development of better anti-anxiety drugs.

evidence.snippet: Synaptically released GABA binds to postsynaptic GABAA receptors, thus causing an influx of negatively charged chloride ions into the postsynaptic neuron.
evidence.explanation: GABA-A receptor activation increases chloride ion influx through the receptor's integral chloride channel.

paper.title: Identification of molecular substrate for the attenuation of anxiety: a step toward the development of better anti-anxiety drugs.

evidence.snippet: This leads to a hyperpolarization and thus functional inhibition of the postsynaptic cell.
evidence.explanation: Chloride influx through the GABA-A channel causes membrane hyperpolarization of the postsynaptic neuron.

paper.title: Identification of molecular substrate for the attenuation of anxiety: a step toward the development of better anti-anxiety drugs.

evidence.snippet: Inhibitory neurotransmission plays a key role in anxiety disorders, as evidenced by the anxiolytic effect of the benzodiazepine class of γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) receptor agonists
evidence.explanation: Membrane hyperpolarization (inhibitory neurotransmission) via GABA-A receptor activation reduces anxiety.

paper.title: Inhibition in the amygdala anxiety circuitry.
